findings.title: A malformed weather-forecast response wedges every later cycle until restart
findings.claim: One weather.get_forecasts response whose forecast holds a non-dict row or is not a list makes every later _async_update_data raise UpdateFailed, even after the weather entity returns a healthy forecast again.
findings.mechanism: _fetch_weather_forecast stores result[entity]['forecast'] into self._weather_forecast (via _forecast_in_model_units, which returns it untouched for a degC/m-s/mm entity) before validating row types; the solar loop then raises AttributeError, which the fetch's except marks as a failed fetch but leaves the stored forecast in place. On the next cycle _update_current_state -> _current_humidity iterates self._weather_forecast with entry.get BEFORE the fetch that would replace it, so the cycle aborts and the fetch is never reached again.

evidence.unit: payloads of 200 whose second cycle (healthy forecast restored) still raises
evidence.machine: B4 cloud container (Linux 6.18, x86_64), CPython 3.14.0rc2, numpy 2.4.6
evidence.contention_note: shared B4 during fan-out; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb row_filter: _forecast_in_model_units wrapped in memory to keep only dict rows of a list ([] for a non-list) where the forecast is stored

findings.metric_definition: Of 200 seeded hostile get_forecasts payloads, count whose second full cycle, with a healthy forecast served again, still raises.
findings.phenomenon_property: A weather forecast the coordinator stores can never make a later cycle fail: whatever a get_forecasts response holds, the stored forecast is a list of dict rows (or the previous/empty forecast), and a healthy response always recovers the next cycle.

null_control.note: same payloads with rows validated at storage: 0 cycles raise

reproduction_steps: Register a weather.get_forecasts handler returning {'weather.home': {'forecast': ['x'] + <48 healthy rows>}}
Run coordinator._async_update_data(): UpdateFailed ('str' object has no attribute 'get')
Serve a healthy forecast and run it again twice: both still raise in _update_current_state -> _current_humidity
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._fetch_weather_forecast: validate forecast is a list and keep only Mapping rows before assigning self._weather_forecast (and treat an empty result as a failed fetch); optionally make _current_humidity/_forecast_arrays tolerate a non-dict row.

findings.title: Finite-but-absurd weather forecast values reach the solve unbounded: failed plans and a runaway solve
findings.claim: A single get_forecasts row with temperature -1e308 makes the plan fail while the cycle reports success, and a single row with wind_speed >= 1e12 makes the real process-worker solve run past a 60 s cap (healthy 3.45 s); clipping the rows where they are stored removes both.
findings.mechanism: No physical-range bound sits between the forecast rows and _forecast_arrays; the arrays go straight to _await_optimize. Wind feeds thermal_model._stability_substeps, whose substep count grows with the wind-driven heat loss, so an absurd wind makes the per-step loop effectively unbounded; an absurd temperature leaves the optimizer no usable start.

evidence.unit: cases of 6 capped at 60 s (wind_1e308_one_row); wind 1e12 and 1e20 also capped in --only runs
evidence.machine: B4 cloud container (Linux 6.18, x86_64), CPython 3.14.0rc2, numpy 2.4.6
evidence.contention_note: shared B4 during fan-out; capped flag is load-robust, wall seconds provisional

perturbation.change: --perturb clip: _forecast_in_model_units wrapped in memory to clip temperature to [-60,60] degC, wind to [0,60] m/s, rain to [0,200] mm

findings.metric_definition: Per poisoned-forecast case, whether one real cycle's solve is still running at the 60 s cap, and its plan status; count of capped cases.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every forecast series handed to the solve is finite and inside a physical range, whatever the weather entity returns.
findings.seam_rule: tools/audit/round9/D1/s2/parsers.py --n 200 (weather.poisoned_series counts the series the solve receives out of range: 8 of 200)

null_control.note: healthy forecast in the same session; wind 500 and 1e6 finish in 1.8 s / 0.9 s

reproduction_steps: Serve a 48-row healthy forecast with row 2 wind_speed=1e12
Run _async_update_data with the real process worker
The solve does not return within 60 s; with --perturb clip it returns optimal in ~3 s
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator: bound temperature/wind/precipitation/irradiance rows to physical ranges (or drop the row) where the forecast is stored; lead to D1-s4 for the unbounded substep count in thermal_model._stability_substeps.

findings.title: A sample count past 2**64 in the thermal-learning store fails every cycle, across restarts
findings.claim: A JSON number >= 2**64 (e.g. 1e20 or 1e308, both accepted by Home Assistant's orjson Store) at cop_baseline[*][1] or capacity_envelope[*][1] makes every cycle raise TypeError in _learning_view.
findings.mechanism: _async_load_thermal_learning / _load_t4b_learners coerce the count with int(entry[1]) and no bound; the resulting Python int exceeds int64 and _learning_view's np.isfinite(entry[1]) raises inside _build_data_dict every cycle. orjson refuses the >64-bit int on re-save, so the corrupt store is never overwritten.

evidence.contention_note: shared B4 during fan-out; counts are contention-immune

findings.phenomenon_property: No value a Home Assistant Store can hand a loader can make a later cycle fail; integer counts from a store are bounded to a range numpy accepts (or the entry is dropped) at load.
findings.seam_rule: tools/audit/round9/D1/s2/store_fuzz.py --sweep-huge (every numeric leaf of every coordinator store)

findings.title: Five cycle-path guards swallow a persistent failure at DEBUG, including pump and frequency actuation
findings.claim: A persistent exception in any of _command_frequency, _async_drive_pumps, _async_watch_learning_drift, _maybe_run_fuse_advisor or _maybe_refresh_price_tile produces zero WARNING-or-above records and zero repair issues over three cycles, while every cycle reports last_update_success=True.
findings.mechanism: The callers fence each callee with `except Exception as err: _LOGGER.debug(...)`, every cycle, with no once-per-cause escalation or repair issue; at default log level the failure is invisible, so a programming error silently stops frequency and pump actuation.

evidence.machine: B4 cloud container (Linux 6.18, x86_64), CPython 3.14.0rc2, numpy 2.4.6
evidence.contention_note: shared B4 during fan-out; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb debug_to_warning: the coordinator logger's debug routed to warning in memory (a guard that logs visibly)

findings.metric_definition: Per guarded callee raising a persistent TypeError, count of WARNING+ log records naming it plus repair issues over 3 cycles; silent_sites = reached sites with 0.
findings.phenomenon_property: A swallowed failure that repeats is visible to the user: at least one WARNING (or a repair issue) per distinct cause, while the cycle still completes.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n -A2 'except Exception' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py | grep _LOGGER.debug (24 guards); harness tools/audit/round9/D1/s2/guards.py drives the 5 on the cycle path
reproduction_steps: last_update_success stays True; only DEBUG 'Pump scheduling skipped' records exist
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator: log the first occurrence of each distinct swallowed cause at WARNING (DEBUG on repeats), as _note_worker_fallback already does; consider a repair issue for the actuation sites.

findings.title: Home Assistant stop waits out an in-flight solve before reaping the solve worker
findings.claim: The EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP listener from async_register_worker_shutdown, fired 0.1 s into a real solve, returns only when the solve does (0.93 of the solve's duration), against 0.008 s with no solve in flight.
findings.mechanism: _shutdown_process_pool takes the module-global _PROCESS_LOCK, which _run_in_process holds for the whole transport round trip (pickle.dump .. pickle.load, i.e. the entire solve). The reap therefore queues behind the solve instead of terminating the child; on a Pi (30-70 s solves, or the D1-s2-02 runaway) that is how long a restart stalls.

evidence.unit: stop latency / solve duration (median of 5; min 0.843, max 1.017)
evidence.machine: B4 cloud container (Linux 6.18, x86_64), CPython 3.14.0rc2, numpy 2.4.6
evidence.contention_note: shared B4 during fan-out, 0 concurrent stress.py; ratio metric, absolutes provisional

perturbation.change: --perturb unlocked_reap: coordinator._PROCESS_LOCK rebound to a fresh Lock for the stop call only (a reap that does not queue behind the transport lock)

findings.metric_definition: Wall time for the stop listener to return when fired 0.1 s into a real coordinator solve, divided by that solve's own duration measured in the same session.
findings.phenomenon_property: Reaping the solve worker at stop never waits for a solve in flight: the stop reap completes in bounded time independent of solve duration.

null_control.note: same listener, same session, no solve in flight

reproduction_steps: Set up an entry on a real loop with a ThreadPoolExecutor
Await the registered EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP listener: it returns when the solve finishes
findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._shutdown_process_pool: grab the worker handle without waiting on the transport lock (or kill the child first so the in-flight pickle.load fails fast), keeping the lock only for the handle swap.

leads.what: Substep count grows without bound with the wind-driven heat loss: one forecast step at wind 1e12 m/s makes a solve run past 60 s (1e6 finishes in 0.9 s). A cap on n_sub (or on the wind it is computed from) would bound a runaway solve whatever the coordinator passes (see D1-s2-02).
A single outdoor-temperature step at -1e308 yields status 'failed (no usable starting point)' rather than a clamped or refused input; the optimizer accepts non-physical but finite forecast series.

Scrubs non-finite leaves but passes finite values that become unrepresentable after the loader's int() (>= 2**64 floats); the store boundary could refuse counts beyond int64 for every store at once (see D1-s2-03).

Parses with stdlib json, which accepts NaN/Infinity tokens and >64-bit integers that Home Assistant's orjson-based Store refuses (whole file quarantined). Fuzz results through the stub include failures that cannot occur in HA; energy 10**400 and defrost duty 10**400 were two.

Calls each async_on_unload callback synchronously and drops a returned coroutine (RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_shutdown' was never awaited, registered by the stub DataUpdateCoordinator); Home Assistant awaits coroutine unload callbacks.

Docstring says the worker 'gets copies, never this object (#1529)', but _diagnose_payload passes coord._last_interval_record by reference (only thermal params are deep-copied). Harmless today (the record is only rebound), but the comment is inaccurate - a D5 comment-accuracy lead.
